forest.statement:
Optimize the supplied baseline on one NVIDIA GH200 with CUDA 12.6.3. Use the real independent AB-MCTS research trees and persistent Mother memory/integration policy. Choose useful topics yourself.
Transpose a square FP32 matrix out of place, writing C[col*n+row]=A[row*n+col]. Performance n=1024, correctness n=32,64,256,1024. Sizes are positive multiples of 32. Output must be bit-exact.
Edit only src/candidate.cu. Preserve the extern C host entry point:
void run(const float*A,const float*B,float*C,float*scratch,int n,int m,int k,float alpha,float beta).
The host provides contiguous device buffers, n=m=k for square matrices, and scratch of at least n*n+65536 floats (64^3+65536 for the derivative). A and B are read-only. C must be fully produced. Do not overwrite any buffer or allocate beyond the declared storage. Scratch contents must not be assumed initialized between calls. The call uses the default CUDA stream; custom device helper functions and multiple launches are allowed. The full run is timed using CUDA events, with allocation, transfers, compilation and correctness checks excluded. Use actual CUDA source, no external optimized math library calls or other resources. Do not read files, environment variables, timers or benchmark state to detect inputs or phases. No persistent cached answers; every invocation must compute its output for the current input. Input dimensions and valid numerical invariants may be specialized.
The driver and oracle are protected. Development harness checks only search inputs; fresh confirmation uses independent seeds. Candidate GPU tests are serialized by the controller. Record failures and measured evidence, integrate after research closes, and independently confirm final G. No new allocations. The published optimized implementations are withheld from the source workspace.

decision.rationale: Lire le source du candidat XOR partagé mesuré pour évaluer une combinaison avec le meilleur candidat vectorisé avant de choisir l’intégration.

Partir du meilleur candidat mesuré et correct de T1 (uint4, 3,142 µs) et lui emprunter le layout XOR 32×32 de 5f05ca36bcd347ee (3,253 µs). Garder les transferts globaux vectorisés et tester le remplacement du tile partagé paddé par l’indexation XOR, sans présumer de gains additifs; préserver la copie bit-exacte et comparer la mesure intégrée au base.

L’intégration mesurée est correcte mais plus lente : 3,294 µs contre 3,142 µs pour cef4bbb63e3e49cf. Les alternatives autonomes observées sont aussi plus lentes et leur combinaison avec le meilleur noyau ne présente pas d’hypothèse additive convaincante. Terminer et laisser le contrôleur sélectionner le meilleur programme validé puis confirmer G indépendamment; cette confirmation n’est pas encore disponible.

retained: Replace the active naive kernel launch with a 32×4-thread block; each warp loads an 8×32 strip, with all lanes loading eight rows at adjacent columns.

Transpose each 8×8 lane/register subgroup through three lane-bit/register-bit exchange stages. Each pair uses a same-warp XOR shuffle with width 8; no cross-warp exchange, shared memory, or CTA barrier is used.
Store the transposed values as eight contiguous floats per subgroup, using unsigned bit-preserving shuffles and float bitcasts for exact copies; use size_t offsets for matrix indexing.

experiments.hypothesis: Four warps per block cover one 32×32 input tile as 8×32 strips. Each lane first owns eight row values for its input column; four 8-lane groups then transpose their 8×8 subtiles by swapping lane/register bits with warp-local XOR shuffles. This should produce coalesced input loads and contiguous 8-float store segments without shared memory or a block barrier.
